transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Derek (CSM), Aisha (Sundance Head of Platform), Tom (CTO), Priya (SRE), Luis (Security)

Summary: brief recap of the 11/11 tail-latency event, where a subset of requests against the hosted cluster experienced 95th+ p99 spikes related to a KV cache invalidation cascade and a scheduling jitter during autoscale. Next steps and owners captured.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll try to keep this tight, we only have 45, 50 minutes. Sorry if there's any background noise on my end. 
[00:18] Aisha: yeah thanks, appreciate it. Tom's on the line too, and Priya will share the staging results later. Luis from security as well. 
[00:25] Tom: hi, thanks, we just want to make sure we don't see that production tail again, okay? That spike hit a couple workflows and cost us some degraded responses. 
[00:35] Connor: quick blind recap from our side: we saw a KV cache eviction followed by a sudden increase in prefix recompute which pushed some requests into slower code-paths; then autoscaler started adding nodes, scheduling jitter caused hot-shard bursts. Not a single point failure but a coupling of factors. 
[01:02] Priya: yep that's what our tracing showed too, though some span names were mangled in the export i.e., the Redwood agent labels came through as 'red-rt' in our collector so mapping was a bit manual. 
[01:18] Derek: just to add, customer observed error rates stayed low, it was primarily latency and some dropped streaming sessions. No data loss. 
[01:30] Luis: from security side we need to confirm what logs are shared and that PII rows are redacted. Also KMS key usage — we need assurance around HSM boundaries. 
[01:50] Maya: understood. Connor, can you pull the per-shard logs and strip any PII? We'll provide a filtered slice. 
[02:00] Connor: yes, plan is to pull slice-level logs for the affected hour window and the adjacent four hours, upload to secure share, and annotate events where cache evictions correlate with p99 increases. 
[02:18] Aisha: timeline wise, we're hoping to have mitigation into staging by next week and then a quick canary. If that passes we'll push to prod. 
[02:30] Tom: also need an estimate on cost impact if we shift the critical flows to Dedicated for a brief window. 
[02:38] Maya: we'll model that and include both steady-state and burst pricing. Expect a short spreadsheet by Friday. 

[03:05] --- Incident deep dive ---
[03:10] Connor: digging in, the main vectors were: 1) an unexpected cache TTL expiration due to a mis-specified workload causing a spike in cache misses; 2) the runtime's fallback branch invoked a heavier attention-kernel path for certain sequence lengths; 3) the autoscaler scaled but scheduling lag created hot-node contention which amplified tail latency. 
[03:42] Priya: sequence length distribution on our traffic changed during a user campaign — more long prompts than baseline which likely bumped the kernel path. We didn't flag that in the alerting. 
[03:55] Derek: sounds like we need both detection (sequence-length drift) and mitigation (fallback routing or pre-warming). 
[04:10] Aisha: could Redwood's routing have shifted traffic to a heavier model variant during the event? 
[04:18] Connor: not automatically—routing policy was stable. There was a fallback to a slightly higher-precision variant when the cache miss rate rose, which is by design for quality preservation, but it increases CPU/GPU per-token cost and can raise latency. 
[04:34] Tom: ok so quality-protection behaviour amplified load. We need knob to opt-out for certain flows. 
[04:42] Maya: yes we suggested a per-route fallback gating flag in previous calls; we'll prioritize a guard that forces a cheaper variant or disabled fallback for your latency-critical routes. 

[05:20] --- Security / Audit questions ---
[05:25] Luis: for the logs that Redwood will share, we need an export showing only service-level telemetry (latency, error rates, shard-id), and we need KMS usage logs for key ops. Does Redwood keep HSM audit trails? 
[05:40] Connor: we keep key operation logs and can provide usage summaries; full HSM audit extracts may require a support ticket, but we can get you the relevant proof-of-use and key rotation times. 
[05:52] Luis: also SSO mapping — when Redwood creates token-level entries, how do we link that to our internal user IDs? We don't want mapping to leak PII. 
[06:05] Maya: we'll provide a sanitized mapping document and advise on best practices for RBAC connectors. 

[06:30] --- Mitigations discussed ---
[06:34] Connor: short-term: 1) gate fallback for latency-critical routes; 2) increase KV cache TTL for targeted prefixes to avoid mass invalidations; 3) prewarm a small Dedicated pool for critical workflows during peak campaigns. 
[06:52] Priya: prewarm sounds good but what's the concurrency headroom we'd need? We had peaks up to 2.4x baseline. 
[07:02] Maya: for a conservative bench we'll recommend capacity for 3x baseline for 10-15 minutes of surge, then autoscale back. We'll size nodes based on your token/sec metrics which we'll ask you to share. 
[07:20] Tom: if we prewarm Dedicated for short windows, what's the minimum billing commitment? 
[07:28] Maya: we can do a temporary dedicated burst plan — there's a short-term burst option charged per-hour at a premium. We'll include that pricing and the delta against hosted in the spreadsheet. 

[08:05] Aisha: an operational ask — can Redwood provide an automated fallback check that runs daily on staging to catch sequence-length shifts? 
[08:14] Connor: we can add a lightweight monitor that samples sequence length distribution and raises an alert when it deviates past a threshold. It'll integrate with your pager. 
[08:24] Priya: perfect, that would have flagged the campaign before production. 

[09:00] --- Discussion on observability gaps ---
[09:06] Derek: we noticed some missing correlation IDs between Redwood traces and Sundance's ingest pipeline; that made root cause slower. 
[09:16] Aisha: yes the trace id mapping was manual. Can we get standardized trace headers? 
[09:22] Connor: we support passing X-Redwood-Trace and a custom header; we'll publish a short doc and sample code. 
[09:30] Luis: include guidance on redaction for those headers so we don't accidentally persist PII. 

[10:05] --- Pragmatic run-through of the runbook ---
[10:10] Maya: quick walkthrough of the emergency rollover: step 1 verify degraded route IDs, step 2 toggle gating flag, step 3 provision prewarm Dedicated pool, step 4 monitor latency for 15 min, step 5 rollback changes if streaming errors increase. Any missing? 
[10:30] Priya: add a sync with DB and cache owners to confirm no TTL-altering jobs are running. We had a maintenance job that overlapped the incident window. 
[10:42] Connor: noted. Also we'll include a 'fail open' checklist: duration thresholds, throughput thresholds, and the exact API call to flip the route gate. 

[11:15] Tom: pricing aside, what's the expected time to implement the gating flag on your side? 
[11:22] Maya: dev-side we can deliver a toggle in about 4 business days, QA and rollout another 2-3 days, but we can push a temporary admin toggle within 24 hours for emergencies. 
[11:34] Aisha: good. We'll want to exercise that admin toggle in a drill. 

[12:00] --- Bench plan ---
[12:05] Connor: propose a 60-minute bench on the Dedicated pool with synthetic workloads matching your recent campaign distribution. We'll run three iterations: baseline on Hosted, Dedicated prewarm, Dedicated sustained for 60 minutes with burst load. We'll capture token latency percentiles and memory/KV stats. 
[12:30] Priya: can you also run with a few long-prompt variations? That was a key variable. 
[12:36] Connor: yes we'll include long sequence tails, and we'll instrument per-kernel time to isolate heavy attention kernels. 

[13:05] Luis: on the compliance deliverables — can you confirm what we will get as machine-readables vs human summaries? We prefer machine-readable logs for SIEM ingestion. 
[13:15] Connor: we'll provide CSV/JSON exports for the telemetry window and a human summary for context. The CSV will have timestamps, shard ids, latency ms, error flags, and anonymized route ids. 
[13:28] Luis: ok, that will help. 

[13:50] --- Risk discussion ---
[13:55] Derek: residual risk is the race between autoscaler convergence and cache re-warm. Our longer-term fix is smarter prefetching and versioned caches. We'll propose a roadmap. 
[14:08] Aisha: timeline on roadmap? We need a rough ETA. 
[14:12] Maya: we'll produce a suggested backlog: immediate fallbacks and TTL tweaks (1-2 weeks), rollout of per-route gating and monitor (2-3 weeks), prefetching and versioned caches (2-3 months) as part of Optimize. 
[14:32] Tom: sounds reasonable. We'll hold Redwood to delivery windows and follow up in a week. 

[15:00] --- Recap and close ---
[15:05] Maya: recapping: Connor to share filtered logs by 11/20; Luis to confirm audit snippet needed by 11/19; Priya to run fallback test by 11/22; Maya to share pricing and runbook by 11/21; bench scheduled for 11/24 pending availability. Follow-up meeting 11/30 to verify mitigations. 
[15:32] Aisha: thanks all, appreciate the quick turn. 
[15:38] Tom: thanks, see you on the bench. 
[15:42] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll upload notes and the action list to the deal in CRM. Bye.

End of transcript.
